THIS BAIL APPLICATION HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 16.11.2023, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 BAIL APPL. NO. 10106 OF 2023 2  ORDER
This is an application for anticipatory bail.

2. Petitioner is the accused in Crime No.1875/2023 of Kalamassery police station, Ernakulam district, alleging commission of offences under Sections 354A(1)(i), 354-B, 376(2)
Xxxxxx vs State Of Kerala on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198656758/
1 (b) and 376(2)(n) of the Indian Penal Code.
3.

Allegation against the petitioner is that, the petitioner while working in the Kerala State Electricity Board (hereinafter referred to as 'the KSEB), had established a relationship with the victim, who was also working in the KSEB and had sexually abused her, by promising to marry her and thereby, the petitioner committed the offences alleged against him.
4. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner would submit that the allegations against the petitioner are absolutely false.

It is submitted that even going by the First Information Statement of the de facto complainant, she became acquainted with the petitioner in the month of December-2018 and she became close with the petitioner.

It is submitted that, according to the de facto complainant/victim, there were some physical contacts between the petitioner and the de facto complainant/victim and finally , in the month of October-2020, there were a break in the relationship between the petitioner and the de facto complainant/victim as the petitioner had informed the de facto complainant/victim that since the petitioner and the de facto complainant/victim belong to different religions, there are some objections to marriage from the parents of the petitioner.

It is submitted that, going by the First Information Statement of the de facto complainant/victim, thereafter, there was no relationship between the petitioner and the de facto complainant/victim till the year 2022.
It is submitted that, according to the de facto complainant/victim, the petitioner again established contact in the year 2022 and again they had some physical contacts.

It is submitted that, going by the First Information Statement itself, the de facto complainant/victim had come to the house of the petitioner on 23.08.2023 knowing that he was about to be married and had created a scene there and picked up a quarrel with the petitioner,
following which the petitioner had filed a complaint before the police and the de facto complainant/victim was taken to the police station.
It is submitted that, it is thereafter that a complaint has been filed on 25.08.2023, leading to registration of Crime No.1875/2023 of Kalamassery police station, raising the allegations as above.

Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner also pointed out that the Sessions Court, while considering the Bail Application of the petitioner found, prima facie, that, on going through the averments in the First Information Statement, the court is doubtful as to whether the offence under Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code would be attracted in this case.
It is submitted that even after finding so, the Sessions Judge did not grant bail to the petitioner since the investigation is at preliminary stage.
It is submitted that if it can be ensured that the petitioner will be co- operating with the investigation, there is no reason to deny anticipatory bail to the petitioner.
5. Learned Public Prosecutor opposes the grant of bail.
It is submitted that, the finding of the Sessions Court that, prima facie the offence under Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code is not attracted, is not sustainable in law.
It is submitted that for the commission of the offence of rape, it is not necessary that penetrative sexual assault must be committed.
It is submitted that the allegations in the First Information Statement are sufficient to attract the offence under Section 376 IPC.

It is submitted that the matter is under investigation and grant of anticipatory bail to the petitioner may not be conducive as admittedly, both the petitioner and the de facto complainant/victim are working under the KSEB.

2 6.

Having heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor and considering the facts and circumstances of the case, I am of the opinion that anticipatory bail can be granted to the petitioner subject to strict conditions.

The allegations against the petitioner, as discernible from the First Information Statement of the de facto complainant/victim, are that the petitioner had sexually abused her by kissing her and touching her on her private parts.

Prima facie,
as rightly found by the Sessions Judge, the statement in the First Information Statement, may not indicate any offence under Section 376 of the IPC in the facts and circumstances of the case.
Both the petitioner as well as the de facto complainant/victim are highly educated and are employees of the KSEB.
The petitioner is not likely to abscond and if the co-operation of the petitioner can be ensured during the course of investigation, there is no reason to deny anticipatory bail to the petitioner.
In the result, this application is allowed.

If any of the aforesaid conditions are violated, the investigating officer in Crime No.1875/2023 of Kalamassery police station may file an application before the jurisdictional court, for cancellation of bail.

Sd/-
